state.jwt: A signed session JWT has not expired. It names identity I and user U. I was revoked before admission instant T, but the check only validates the JWT signature and expiry.
state.aba: The first fresh read sees operator source position 7 and active=true. Between first and second read, revoke then regrant both commit. The second read sees position 9 and active=true.
state.pass: The authority reads fixed sources identity I, operator O, and policy P in first pass. All first reads finish. It samples trusted time T. Then it freshly reads exactly I, O, and P again. Each source returns the same non-resettable physical position and generation as in the first pass. Every veto-changing fact advances its respective position.
state.changed: The first identity read finds I attached to U at position 4. I is revoked before T, then the second fresh identity read observes position 5. The operator grant remains active throughout.
state.wronguser: A cryptographically valid credential names an identity attached to user U. The criteria intent claims a different operator user V.
state.expired: A validly signed token has raw expiration time earlier than T, though it was unexpired when request processing began.
state.expirelater: All required authorization sources are valid at T and the raw credential has not expired at T. The credential expires after T but before the already-admitted exact operation finishes.
state.stale_policy: The active authoritative access policy is generation 2. A worker only knows its local binary implements generation 1 and reads no authoritative generation source.
state.missing: Identity and operator reads are valid but a required session revocation owner is unavailable; the policy requires that owner as a veto.
state.retry: The first attempt passes only the first-pass reads but fails before completing the second pass. A later retry runs using an old saved allow flag without new reads.

jwt_authorizes.instructions: In jwt, may the revoked identity be admitted at T solely because the JWT is signed and unexpired?

aba_equal.instructions: In aba, does identical active=true prove the source did not change between reads?

pass_common.instructions: Given every stated assumption in pass, did the three source states all hold together at T?

changed_allow.instructions: In changed, may the two-pass proof accept the earlier identity state despite its changed position?

wronguser_allow.instructions: In wronguser, may the authenticated identity for U authorize an operator intent as V?

expired_allow.instructions: In expired, was the credential valid at T under a strict raw expiration rule?

expirelater_cancel.instructions: Under an admission-at-T policy, does expirelater automatically cancel the already-admitted operation?

localpolicy_proves.instructions: In stale_policy, does the local binary version prove it used the current authoritative policy?

missing_allow.instructions: In missing, is the required veto satisfied merely because its owner was unavailable?

retry_allow.instructions: In retry, does the old incomplete first pass establish a fresh current admission on retry?

provider_proven.instructions: Do the stated two-pass assumptions by themselves prove the deployed sources actually have linearizable reads and non-resettable positions?
